name: Canvas Design
description: Creates original static artwork such as posters or covers as PNG or PDF, using a visual concept to guide composition, texture, and typography.
requirements: The artifact size, intended viewing distance, exact text, output format, and any artwork that may be incorporated.
steps: Describe the idea the viewer should take away and the practical limits of the design.
Request an original composition in the target dimensions. Render or export it and review the visual at its final size.
example: Design an A4 poster for a fictional night-bird count. The poster must say ‘Night Chorus’, ‘14 June’, and ‘Meet at Willow Gate’. Use layered silhouettes to convey listening after dark and deliver a print PDF.
check: Open the PDF, check the page size, verify all three text strings, and inspect the smallest lettering at print size.

name: DIVI WordPress Editing
description: Guides edits to WordPress sites built with Divi, including module changes, template adjustments, performance work, and migration planning.
requirements: The Divi version, the page or template to change, a staging copy or exported layout, and access appropriate to the task.
steps: Identify whether the change belongs to an individual module, a shared template, or a child theme. Save a copy of the affected layout.
Apply the change in staging and inspect other pages that inherit the same shared element.
example: On our staging Divi site, change the summer course page to show the enrollment module before testimonials on phones. Keep the desktop order and list any changes to shared templates.
check: Inspect the updated page in Divi Builder and the front end at both widths, then open a second page using the same template.

name: imagegen-frontend-mobile
description: Uses image generation to visualize mobile app screens from a product brief, producing mockups for pitches and product discussions.
requirements: An image-generation capability, target device or aspect ratio, screen content, and reference assets the project can use.
steps: Specify the user task, platform, screen hierarchy, and exactly which text must appear.
Generate a reference screen, inspect it at phone size, and carry the approved visual direction into subsequent states.
example: Generate two portrait mockups for a bike locker app. Show a locker selection screen and a reservation confirmation, using the same header, type scale, and small map legend in both.
check: Check the screen dimensions, labels, and continuity between screens. Read the mockups at actual display size before presenting them.

name: Algorithmic Art
description: Creates generative art in p5.js, with a short artistic premise, adjustable parameters, and a random seed that can reproduce a composition.
requirements: A visual idea, the parameters worth exploring, and a browser able to run the generated viewer and load its p5.js dependency.
steps: Describe the visual system in terms of forces, geometry, rhythm, or repetition.
Request the algorithm and viewer with controls for a few meaningful parameters and a seed. Explore a variation and return to the original seed.
example: Build a p5.js study of tidal channels branching across sand. Let me vary branch density and flow direction, and make seed 247 recover the same starting image.
check: Reload the viewer with seed 247 and the same settings, compare the result, then adjust a single parameter to verify that the change is visible.
